data.name: Tally Ho
data.detailed_description:
Only a perfect servant can solve a perfect mess! Being the perfect gentleman's gentleman or lady's lady doesn't make you an angel. Can you untangle your employer's knottiest problems with elegance and unruffled grace? As the valet or lady's maid of Rory Wintermint, you'll go head to head with recalcitrant aunts, light-handed houseguests, manage a fox hunt and corral exotic birds!

Tally Ho is a 600,000 word interactive comedy of manners by Kreg Segall, where your choices control the story. It's entirely text-based—without graphics or sound effects—and fueled by the vast, unstoppable power of your imagination.

It's England between the wars, and the 1920s are roaring! When your employer, a proper young gentleman or lady named Rory Wintermint is summoned to their aunt Primrose's country house Ritornello for a weekend, it's up to you to make everything run smoothly...or not! Glide gracefully behind the scenes to arrange everything from the flowers to their love life, or leave Rory to their own devices as you pursue crime, adventure, and romance! Will you lie, cheat, and steal to ensure your employer's happiness, or will you insist upon personal integrity?

  • Play as male, female, or nonbinary; gay, straight, or bi, and even poly.
  • Help Rory sort out their love life, or sabotage it utterly.
  • Solve the case of a mysterious sneak-thief--or join them on a crime spree.
  • Aid spies, evade the law, calm flighty flappers, and unruffle Aunt Primrose.
  • Win an Exotic Animal Show and a boat race fairly, or cheat!
  • Dance the lindy hop, or a graceful waltz—or just tut disapprovingly.
  • Ride trains, motorcycles, zip-lines, bicycles, horses, and rusty jalopies!
  • Jazz it up in the Jazz Age, or remain aloof and cool as a cucumber.

You'll be swinging from the chandeliers or serving the canapes in this madcap, but altogether elegant comedy.

reviews.review:
As with all these Choice-of-Games games, whether you'll like it or not depends mostly upon interest in the premise and the writing talent of the author.  As usual, there's a demo that can give you enough of both to let you see whether you'll be interested in shelling out for more.  

As far as the premise goes... I'm just left wondering why on earth nobody did this sooner?!  There's a glut of superhero and D&D-type Choice-of-Games, but while there's a few (quite good, as well) Jules Verne/steampunk-flavored games out there, just straight-up going for the foppery of the old British upper class is virgin territory.  Playing as an impossibly talented and dedicated butler or maid trying to save an utter wastrel from themselves wasn't something I'd thought I'd needed until I knew it existed, but now I can't live without it. 

So far as the writing goes, it clearly takes its digs at the era, but without getting into overtly acerbic territory.  It's lighthearted comedic fair, and while it has some moments of it (character speech is era-appropriate, but the narration is more modern casual), the text lacks consistent flourishes of supersilious wit more of the purple prose of the era might have.  Whether that's good or bad is up to you, since intentional loquciousness would undoubtably unnerve some readers, but it feels to me like a missed opportunity to spice up the more obviously comedic passages with some of the language of the penny dreadfuls that would help set the mood of the entire genre this game plays up as its setting.

As a butler or maid, you are a member of the most-definitely-not-invisible servantry.  To attain that prestigious post, you naturally have a background in some presumably vastly more lucrative field that logic would imply requires more skilled training than mopping the floors, such as art gallery curator, professional boxer, lion tamer, or international jewel thief. This informal training is just barely enough to qualify you for your baseline duties as a member of the servantry, such as cooking, cleaning, tutoring your master and their family's young ones, backtalking your master and his/her guests, fisticuffs with ruffians, sabotaging police investigations, jailbreaking, assuming control over police investigations in spite of being a vigilante, participating in espionage on behalf of an international housekeeping syndicate, directly controlling the fate of your employer's dynasty, and participating in contests in quaint county fairs.  

Please be advised that it is frowned upon in upright, dignified upperclass families of the era for a a gentleman's gentleman or lady's lady to seduce their same-sex employer, or to steal their fiance out from under their noses, but for gentlemen and ladies of extraordinary talent and poise (you get a 'score' stat for succeeding at skill checks that are required for some endings), some eyes may wind up turned.
